questions.q: How does Event Monitoring differ in scope from a debug log captured via a trace flag?
options: They capture exactly the same data, just in different file formats
Event Monitoring only works in sandboxes, never in production orgs
A debug log captures org-wide activity, while Event Monitoring captures only one transaction at a time
A debug log captures one specific transaction you deliberately reproduced; Event Monitoring captures user and system activity continuously across the whole org, without requiring a trace flag
questions.explain: A debug log is scoped to one transaction you set a trace flag to capture; Event Monitoring is an always-on, org-wide capture of activity, which is what makes it suited to a different class of diagnostic question.

questions.q: What is the key practical difference between Event Log Files and Real-Time Event Monitoring?
options: Event Log Files only exist in Developer Edition orgs; Real-Time Event Monitoring only exists in production
They are two names for the exact same mechanism with no actual difference

Event Log Files are delivered asynchronously (events can take up to an hour to appear) and suit retrospective analysis; Real-Time Event Monitoring is built on platform events for catching activity as it happens
Real-Time Event Monitoring replaced Event Log Files entirely and Event Log Files no longer exist
questions.explain: Event Log Files are asynchronous and better for retrospective, trend-style analysis; Real-Time Event Monitoring is platform-events-based and suited to catching something as it's actively happening.

questions.q: What data retention does Salesforce's own documentation state for Event Monitoring log file types in a Developer Edition org?
options: No access to Event Monitoring data at all in Developer Edition
Free access to all log types, with 1-day data retention
Full access with 1-year retention, identical to a paid production add-on
30-day retention, the same as debug logs
questions.explain: Trailhead's Event Monitoring documentation states that Developer Edition orgs get free access to all log types but with only 1-day data retention — enough to explore the feature, not for serious historical trend analysis.

questions.q: Why can a debug log fail to capture an intermittent or rarely-reported performance problem, where Event Monitoring might succeed?
options: A debug log only exists for a transaction someone deliberately set a trace flag to capture, so an intermittent issue nobody thought to reproduce under a trace flag will likely never show up in one; Event Monitoring's always-on capture doesn't depend on anyone noticing first
Debug logs are disabled by default in all orgs and must be purchased separately
Event Monitoring and debug logs capture identical data, so this isn't actually a meaningful difference
Debug logs can only capture Flow activity, never Apex activity
questions.explain: Debug logs require someone to deliberately capture a specific transaction, so a problem that's intermittent or never gets reported won't be caught. Event Monitoring's continuous, org-wide capture doesn't depend on anyone noticing the issue first.

questions.q: Why is recommending Event Monitoring as an ongoing practice (not just a one-time debug session) considered an architect-level recommendation?
options: Because only architects are permitted to view Event Monitoring data under Salesforce's licensing terms
Because Event Monitoring requires custom Apex code to function, unlike debug logs
Because Event Monitoring is only available in a special Architect edition of Salesforce

Because it supports identifying slow patterns across hundreds of transactions over time, catching problems long before an individual user complaint would surface them, which is a governance-level concern beyond fixing one reported bug
questions.explain: Recommending always-on, org-wide monitoring as a standing practice (rather than reacting one bug at a time) reflects the kind of forward-looking, governance-oriented thinking a Technical Architect is expected to bring, distinct from simply fixing whatever ticket is open today.
